text.tspan: 412 from the flush script
the precondition failed: the file changed
on the server since we based our edit on it
FileIo the cached base version
the copy the edit started from

g.text: Net GET the server's current version, with its ETag

text.tspan: 3-way merge — pure, no I/O
base, ours, theirs
Net PUT the merge — conditional on exactly the
version it was merged from.
Unconditional here would silently discard a third
change that landed between our GET and this PUT:
the very lost update this machinery exists to prevent

g.text: DbWrite the new ETag and size
FileIo store the merged bytes in the cache

text.tspan: resolved — auto-merged, and the user
never had to know
412 again — the server moved on while we were
merging, so the merge is stale
Net PUT a conflicted copy
under a timestamped name, with If-None-Match: *
The name has one-second resolution, so a second
conflict in the same second must not overwrite the
first copy — asserting the name is free is what
prevents that

g.text: a de-duplicated name — at most four attempts

text.tspan: Fail — every candidate name taken
Vanishingly unlikely, and safe: the buffer is kept,
so the content is retried rather than dropped
tell the user where their edit went
Their bytes are safe, but under a name they would
not otherwise find. The original keeps the server's
version

g.text: invalidate listings taken before the copy landed

text.tspan: Net PROPFIND the parent
so the copy appears beside the original
back to the flush script
drop the buffer, desktop indicator → Idle, Answer OK
This also covers a deferred create that lost the race
against a same-named file created on the server: its
If-None-Match: * failed, and there is no merge base,
so the copy path runs. The local content survives
under the copy name and the reload brings in theirs
